hypotheses.description: Demand reduction exists under the implemented lowest-accepted-bid uniform pricing: reducing reported quantity strictly raises a multi-unit bidder's integer surplus.
hypotheses.key_finding: 2-bidder 2-unit witness: truthful (q=2 @ 100) makes the bidder's own bid pivotal (clearing 100, surplus 0); reducing to q=1 lets the rival's 60 set the clearing price (surplus 40). Strict for every rival price 1..99.

hypotheses.description: Single-unit bidding is not truthful: a pivotal winner pays its own bid, so shading to runner-up + 1 strictly profits.
hypotheses.key_finding: 1-unit witness with value 100 vs runner-up 60: truthful surplus 0; the shade sweep 61..100 confirms surplus = 100 - shade, maximized at shade = 61 with strict gain 39.

hypotheses.description: Price ties are grindable: the (-price, commitment, bidder_id) sort key makes tie wins purchasable with a handful of sha256 nonce trials, and the tie value is strictly positive.
hypotheses.key_finding: Tie witness at price 80, value 100: winner takes 20, loser 0; deterministic nonce grinding flips the settlement winner. Best-of-T own digests beats min-of-m rivals at the exchangeability rate T/(T+m) (measured within 9 points of 1/2 at T=m for m in {1,3,7}); each trial costs one hash. Note the trials-to-win distribution is heavy-tailed (E[1/U_min] diverges for m=1), so evidence is stated as a win-rate law, not an expected-trials claim.

hypotheses.description: The maximum admissible non-reveal bond (MAX_BOND = 65535) is below the adverse-move option value for every quantity q >= 2, so no admissible bond forces reveal of multi-unit commitments.
hypotheses.key_finding: Two-layer coverage: exhaustive threshold arithmetic over every q in 2..MAX_UNITS (delta = MAX_BOND//q + 1 stays in-domain, q*delta > MAX_BOND >= q*(delta-1)), plus real settle+bond payoff binding for q in 2..16 where slashing (-65535) strictly beats revealing (-q*delta) and one unit less adverse flips it (exact threshold). Boundary refinement: at q = 1 the worst in-domain loss is 65534 < 65535, so the max bond does force reveal for single-unit commitments.

hypotheses.description: Commit-then-reveal-iff-favorable beats always-reveal exactly when quantity * support-width exceeds the bond: the commitment is a free option past that threshold.
hypotheses.key_finding: Two-point support sim through the real settlement and bond functions: conditional - always = q*w - b exactly for all widths 1..40 and bonds 1..80 at q=2 (strictly better when q*w > b, equal at q*w = b, worse below).

hypotheses.description: Self-competition pinning: one bidder submitting a second, worthless decoy commitment can lower the clearing price it pays on its real units.
hypotheses.key_finding: 4-units-for-sale witness: honest A (2 @ 100 vs rival 1 @ 90) pays clearing 90 (payoff 20); adding a decoy 1 @ d under the same bidder_id makes d the clearing price, payoff 200 - 3d (strictly better for d < 60, indifferent at 60); d = 1 yields payoff 197. The mechanism admits repeated bidder_id without aggregation.
